results.description: The Buffalo Bills' offense, when led by Josh Allen, has fared extremely well in each of its last three games against the Los Angeles Rams. Here are four player prop bets that bank on the Bills piling up the yards and points on primetime.
highlights: Oct 4, 2026; Orchard Park, New York, USA;  Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen (17) looks to pass during the third quarter against the New England Patriots at New Highmark Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect James Cook 100+ rush yards (+235) Cook ranks second amongst NFL leaders in yards per carry (6.0), and he's been highly efficient each of the past three weeks. After rushing for 135 and 154 yards, respectively, in Weeks 2 and 3, the Bills mistakenly moved away from Cook at times during the Week 4 loss. Having totaled 45 rushes over the prior two games, he carried only 12 times for 75 yards against the Patriots. As a result, I'm expecting the Bills to feed Cook as often as possible against the Rams, who allow 102.0 rush yards per game. He went over the 100-yard mark in more than 50 percent of games last season, and I'm looking for him to repeat that feat on Monday night.

Oct 4, 2026; Orchard Park, New York, USA;  Buffalo Bills wide receiver Keon Coleman (0) makes a catch for a touchdown as New England Patriots cornerback Charles Woods (22) defends  | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dalton Kincaid Anytime touchdown scorer (+185) Maybe I'm a glutton for punishment, considering I also took Kincaid to score 8+ touchdowns for the season, but I'm not giving up yet. With his first, and only, touchdown this season coming on primetime against the Detroit Lions in Week 2, let's back Kincaid to find pay dirt again on Monday Night Football. It also seems as if the Bills will make it a point to target Kincaid as often as possible after failing to get him into the flow against the New England Patriots in Week 4.

Oct 4, 2026; Orchard Park, New York, USA;  Buffalo Bills running back James Cook (4) runs after making a catch during the third quarter against the New England Patriots | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Keon Coleman 50+ receiving yards (+143) Coleman stepped up in a big way when DJ Moore was forced out of the game against the Patriots. He has at least one 20+ yard reception in each of the past three games, and his big play ability makes the 50-yard mark even more attainable. Additionally, Coleman, who has Allen's trust, should be a significant factor for an offense that will be without wide receiver Josh Palmer and potentially Moore, too.
